notes: Governing document: the UNO AAUP agreement in force on the reference date (2017-19) is not saved. Following the documented bracketing decision (version note of 2018_02), the 2015-17 agreement is coded where it reads the same as the 2019-21 successor; a word-level diff of section 3.9 (Leaves) and Attachment B (NU Parental Leave Policies) found them substantively identical (3.9.3.2 in 2019-21 adds that medical information goes to Human Resources; 3.9.1.1 wording 'eligible to apply for' -> 'eligible for'). Every component citing 2018_02 carries version_uncertain. The 2018_02 version note's example of a successor-only provision ('2019-21 s3.9.5.2') is in fact present in 2015-17 too (3.9.5.2, family/medical leave in conjunction with parental leave). The 2015-17 text's own 5.1 still gives the 2013-15 term (stale clause); 3.6.4 gives 2015-17.

No-policy check (`missing`): missing = false, because a governing faculty leave document covering tenure-stream faculty is saved: the bracketing 2015-17 agreement (accepted for the reference date by the documented decision) and NU Executive Memorandum No. 18 (a tenure-clock policy in force on the reference date). The agreement in force (2017-19) is the missing governing document.

Sources: 2018_00_link is a generic UNO HR page (captured 2019-08-17) summarising FMLA, the staff sick leave policy and maternity/adoption sick leave; its staff provisions are coded summary_only (c20, c21); its adoption line ('UNO allows eight weeks of sick leave time. Male employees may be eligible for the eight weeks of paid sick leave.') restates Attachment B's adoption leave for staff and is not a separate component. 2018_01 is an undated Academic Affairs summary quoting the 2017-19 agreement's 3.9.3.5.a verbatim, identical to the 2015-17 and 2019-21 text, which supports continuity of c17. 2018_04 is NU Executive Memorandum No. 18 (1999), system-wide.

Birth parent chain: relief from instruction for the semester containing the leave (c4, discretion-flagged) contains Medical Maternity Leave 8 weeks normally, paid at full salary (c2, within c4); Disability Leave up to 6 months (c1) starts with it, its salary within it (c3, up to 6 months); FMLA 12 workweeks alongside from the start (c9); then Personal Leave up to 1 year while a documented disability exists (c12, consecutive_after c1), or a part-time return up to 12 months (c13).

Non-birth parent chain: Paternal Leave up to 5 days paid (c5), FMLA 12 workweeks alongside from the start (c9); then, discretionary, the semester extension of family/medical leave (c10, consecutive_after c9; no length coded) and the exceptional personal leave (c11, consecutive_after c10) within the one-year combined limit (leave_limits).

Pay route for faculty: Attachment B charges childbirth disability, paternal and adoption leave to 'sick leave or disability leave depending on the employee's appointment category'; unit members have Disability Leave (CBA 3.9.3, salary up to six months per leave). Coded as an employer plan (R1), flagged on c3 because 3.9.5.3(d) speaks of 'accrued, unused ... disability leave'. If Disability Leave were read as an own balance, c2, c5, c6 and c7 would take payer own_balance (R1b).

Documents cited but not saved: the 2017-19 UNO AAUP agreement; the University of Nebraska Family/Medical Leaves of Absence Policy; the UNO Family Medical Leave Policy and the Crisis Leave Sharing Program (HR page links); the University Sick Leave Policy; the campus written policy statement for parental leave approval; the Bylaws of the Board of Regents (3.4.3.3, 4.1, 4.10, 4.8, 4.11, 4.14); the UNUM Long-term Disability Income Protection Policy; the Faculty Workload Assignment Policy (1991); Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-234.

Not components: Faculty Development Fellowship and Professional Leave Without Pay (3.9.1; professional purposes only, which a parent cannot use for a birth); Administrative Leave With Pay (3.9.6; weather and operations); funeral leave (named only); discretionary family/medical leave for a sibling's health condition (not a parent's need).
Statutory floor (U7): FMLA, 12 workweeks, applies; no Nebraska baseline rows exist in statutory_baseline.csv.
